http://lmss.sali.org/RDIT4CoYkPzMDC1y2RD.label: Antitrust - Vertical Price Fixing Claims
http://lmss.sali.org/RDIT4CoYkPzMDC1y2RD.definition: An allegation of illegal collusion between parties at different levels of a supply chain to set prices for goods or services, in violation of antitrust laws.

http://lmss.sali.org/RDITNZvakvvHzO0cOV5.label: Matter Total Detail Fees
http://lmss.sali.org/RDITNZvakvvHzO0cOV5.definition: Matter Total Detail Fees refers to the specific fees associated with a particular legal matter, including all costs and expenses incurred in providing legal services, as defined within the context of Engagement Terms.

http://lmss.sali.org/RDITWdJs6lzS28lvVyM.label: Executor Plaintiff
http://lmss.sali.org/RDITWdJs6lzS28lvVyM.definition: An executor of an estate who is also the plaintiff in a legal matter.

http://lmss.sali.org/RDIcTaDzu8L9eXSdZX6.label: Enforceability Representation
http://lmss.sali.org/RDIcTaDzu8L9eXSdZX6.definition: Enforceability Representation: A statement made in a legal agreement that assures the parties involved that the terms of the agreement can be enforced by law.

http://lmss.sali.org/RDIdtcSi09CZtgL1n55.label: Georgia Superior Court - Decatur County
http://lmss.sali.org/RDIdtcSi09CZtgL1n55.definition: A court of general jurisdiction in Georgia that has authority over civil and criminal cases within Decatur County.

http://lmss.sali.org/RDIgqpnkyBP3BzrGZfw.label: Unemployment Benefits Law
http://lmss.sali.org/RDIgqpnkyBP3BzrGZfw.definition: Law governing the entitlement to and payment of financial assistance to individuals who have lost their jobs, including eligibility requirements, benefit calculations, duration of support, employer contributions, and the administrative processes for claiming and managing unemployment benefits.

http://lmss.sali.org/RDIh20HdkrzKjC0i3O7.label: Compact Clause Claim
http://lmss.sali.org/RDIh20HdkrzKjC0i3O7.definition: A Compact Clause claim is a legal argument asserting that a particular agreement or compact between states or between a state and a foreign power violates the Compact Clause of the United States Constitution. This claim contends that the agreement or compact exceeds the scope of authority granted by the Compact Clause, which requires congressional approval for interstate compacts that impact the balance of power between states or have implications for federal supremacy.

http://lmss.sali.org/RDIhCFQBOYix4MdT4Rs.label: Motion for Appointment of Pro Bono Counsel
http://lmss.sali.org/RDIhCFQBOYix4MdT4Rs.definition: A Motion for Appointment of Pro Bono Counsel is a formal request made to the court by a party who cannot afford an attorney, asking the court to appoint a volunteer lawyer to represent them in the case.

http://lmss.sali.org/RDIn866adG12xMovtJF.label: Massachusetts Superior Court - Middlesex County
http://lmss.sali.org/RDIn866adG12xMovtJF.definition: The Massachusetts Superior Court - Middlesex County is a court of general jurisdiction in Massachusetts that hears civil and criminal cases within Middlesex County.

http://lmss.sali.org/RDIuHPBKs3x9tZ0vRBJ.label: Procedural Claims
http://lmss.sali.org/RDIuHPBKs3x9tZ0vRBJ.definition: Procedural Claims are legal claims that relate to the process of a lawsuit, such as jurisdiction, venue, or intervention, rather than the substantive issues of the case.

http://lmss.sali.org/RDIwFaFcH4KY0gwEY0Q.label: Industry
http://lmss.sali.org/RDIwFaFcH4KY0gwEY0Q.definition: An economic branch that produces a related set of raw materials, goods, or services (e.g., Agriculture Industry, Pharmaceuticals Industry).

http://lmss.sali.org/RDJ49Jely64COWJAZS6.label: Immigrant Visa for Intercountry Adoption of Orphan Children by Citizen of Host Country
http://lmss.sali.org/RDJ49Jely64COWJAZS6.definition: "Visa for Intercountry Adoption of Orphan Children by Citizen of Host Country" involves the legal process whereby a citizen adopts a foreign-born orphan, granting the child residency and eventually citizenship rights. This adoption type includes visas specifically designated for orphans in need of permanent care and typically ensures compliance with international adoption regulations, including the Hague Convention.

http://lmss.sali.org/RDJ5gLF3diEDjeGSux0.label: Undersecured Creditor
http://lmss.sali.org/RDJ5gLF3diEDjeGSux0.definition: An Undersecured Creditor is a lender whose collateral value securing a loan is less than the outstanding debt owed by the borrower. This situation often arises in bankruptcy contexts, affecting the creditor’s ability to fully recover the loan amount through collateral liquidation.

http://lmss.sali.org/RDJ9jbKtSOU0ZiD1spY.label: Motion to Dismiss for Lack of Subject Matter Jurisdiction
http://lmss.sali.org/RDJ9jbKtSOU0ZiD1spY.definition: A Motion to Dismiss for Lack of Subject Matter Jurisdiction is a legal request to terminate a case due to the court lacking the authority to hear and decide on the specific legal matter at hand.

http://lmss.sali.org/RDJGO2CCArhfhsh9diM.label: Official Immunity
http://lmss.sali.org/RDJGO2CCArhfhsh9diM.definition: Official Immunity: Legal protection granted to government officials from being held personally liable for actions taken in the course of their official duties.

http://lmss.sali.org/RDJGZMiDpzOg0usYKbb.label: Kansas District Court - Labette County, Oswego
http://lmss.sali.org/RDJGZMiDpzOg0usYKbb.definition: A court located in Labette County, Oswego, Kansas that has jurisdiction over certain legal matters within its geographical area.

http://lmss.sali.org/RDJHR4WqMpTsR6pGC2f.label: Travel Document Valid From
http://lmss.sali.org/RDJHR4WqMpTsR6pGC2f.definition: The "Travel Document Valid From" date indicates the starting date from which a travel document such as a passport or visa becomes legally valid for use. This date may differ from the issued date and marks the beginning of the period during which the holder is authorized to travel under the conditions specified by the document

http://lmss.sali.org/RDJKYhVrQurg0zQmBql.label: Post-Petition Transfer Claim
http://lmss.sali.org/RDJKYhVrQurg0zQmBql.definition: A post-petition transfer claim is a type of avoidance action claim in bankruptcy law that seeks to recover property or assets transferred by a debtor after the filing of a bankruptcy petition.

http://lmss.sali.org/RDJM7d52FqDzFaBbtRd.label: Limitations
http://lmss.sali.org/RDJM7d52FqDzFaBbtRd.definition: The concept of Limitations refers to the legal time constraints that restrict the period within which a party can bring a claim or defense in a civil litigation matter, including statutes of repose, frauds, and limitations, equitable tolling, and laches.

http://lmss.sali.org/RDJPhq9RjJu1rvptoQK.label: Airplane
http://lmss.sali.org/RDJPhq9RjJu1rvptoQK.definition: An Airplane is a powered fixed-wing aircraft that achieves flight through the use of forward thrust and aerodynamic lift. It typically has a fuselage, wings, and one or more engines, and is designed for transporting passengers, cargo, or both.

http://lmss.sali.org/RDJUDQGYk9rhdIFXzTy.label: Substantive Due Process Claim
http://lmss.sali.org/RDJUDQGYk9rhdIFXzTy.definition: A substantive due process claim is a legal action initiated by an individual or entity alleging that their fundamental rights, as protected by the Due Process Clauses of the Fifth and Fourteenth Amendments of the United States Constitution, have been violated by the government or a government actor. Substantive due process protects individuals from arbitrary or unreasonable government actions that infringe on fundamental rights, even if proper procedures were followed. A substantive due process claim may arise in various contexts, such as when a government body enacts a law or regulation that unduly restricts a fundamental right (e.g., the right to privacy, the right to marry, or the right to make decisions about family matters) or when a government actor takes an arbitrary or irrational action that infringes on an individual's rights.

http://lmss.sali.org/RDJWZSnQkLCRb0PTCaf.label: Georgia District Court - Dougherty County
http://lmss.sali.org/RDJWZSnQkLCRb0PTCaf.definition: A court located in Dougherty County, Georgia that has jurisdiction over certain legal matters within its geographical boundaries.

http://lmss.sali.org/RDJWZaJFpjsPgcq6eYi.label: Joy
http://lmss.sali.org/RDJWZaJFpjsPgcq6eYi.definition: Joy is an emotion of great pleasure or happiness, often resulting from success, good fortune, or a sense of well-being.

http://lmss.sali.org/RDJYLQ3woaBs6FkT7wM.label: Wrongful Discharge or Termination
http://lmss.sali.org/RDJYLQ3woaBs6FkT7wM.definition: The concept of Wrongful Discharge or Termination refers to the illegal firing or dismissal of an employee by an employer, in violation of the law or employment contract.

http://lmss.sali.org/RDJc44Ilo9XW8Y74blN.label: Supplemental Jurisdiction
http://lmss.sali.org/RDJc44Ilo9XW8Y74blN.definition: Supplemental Jurisdiction refers to the authority of a court to hear and decide on claims that are related to the original claim, but may not fall under the court's primary jurisdiction.

http://lmss.sali.org/RDJcJ6zr1Q6V6fF7cMy.label: Motion for Royalty
http://lmss.sali.org/RDJcJ6zr1Q6V6fF7cMy.definition: A Motion for Royalty is a formal request made to a trial court for compensation or ongoing payment for the use of intellectual property.

http://lmss.sali.org/RDJdE3YoLZbldxnPJMY.label: Contact Full Name
http://lmss.sali.org/RDJdE3YoLZbldxnPJMY.definition: Contact Full Name refers to the complete legal name of an individual serving as a point of contact in professional or business interactions. This often includes the person's first name, middle name or initial, and last name, and is used for formal documentation and communication.

http://lmss.sali.org/RDJgy4NDLgsP7qaqied.label: Interactive Media
http://lmss.sali.org/RDJgy4NDLgsP7qaqied.definition: Interactive Media refers to digital content that requires user interaction to deliver its content, such as video games, virtual reality experiences, and interactive websites. Protected under copyright law, interactive media grants the creators exclusive rights to reproduce, distribute, and display the content.

http://lmss.sali.org/RDJpP80M638JNtaUBT7.label: Proceeding Transferred Into This Dispute Forum
http://lmss.sali.org/RDJpP80M638JNtaUBT7.definition: The concept of "Case Transferred Into This Dispute Forum" refers to a legal matter that has been moved from another forum to the current forum for resolution, and is currently open or pending.

http://lmss.sali.org/RDJqeqCuDHyFSnpfHfm.label: Warranty
http://lmss.sali.org/RDJqeqCuDHyFSnpfHfm.definition: A Warranty is a promise or guarantee provided by a manufacturer or seller to the buyer concerning the quality, condition, or functionality of a product for a specified period. If the product fails to meet the stipulated conditions during the warranty period, the manufacturer or seller is obliged to repair, replace, or refund the product.

http://lmss.sali.org/RDJrTFbZzszQTzfaqdD.label: Minangkabau
http://lmss.sali.org/RDJrTFbZzszQTzfaqdD.definition: A language spoken in the Minangkabau region of Indonesia, characterized by its unique matrilineal culture and use of a modified Arabic script.

http://lmss.sali.org/RDJrxrj7NP4TJBZS8rg.label: D.C. Board on Professional Responsibility
http://lmss.sali.org/RDJrxrj7NP4TJBZS8rg.definition: The D.C. Board on Professional Responsibility is a disciplinary body within the District of Columbia Courts that oversees the conduct of lawyers practicing in the District of Columbia.

http://lmss.sali.org/RDJssYq6dD0i6zlieP3.label: Crewmember Visa
http://lmss.sali.org/RDJssYq6dD0i6zlieP3.definition: A Crewmember Visa is a specific type of visa issued to individuals who work on board a sea vessel or international airline, such as pilots, flight attendants, or ship crew members. This visa allows the holder to enter and stay in a foreign country for a limited period, strictly for the purpose of joining, working on, or disembarking from their vessel or aircraft.

http://lmss.sali.org/RDJvfvUzCUfCqBqkpPj.label: Failure to Yield to Pedestrian Claim
http://lmss.sali.org/RDJvfvUzCUfCqBqkpPj.definition: A Pedestrian Right-of-Way Violation Claim involves allegations that a driver has failed to yield the right-of-way to pedestrians under circumstances where pedestrians are legally prioritized, such as crosswalks or signals.

http://lmss.sali.org/RDJwYAhLKCUFLjsFuAC.label: Liquor Law Violations
http://lmss.sali.org/RDJwYAhLKCUFLjsFuAC.definition: The violation of laws or ordinances prohibiting the manufacture, sale, purchase, transportation, possession, or use of alcoholic beverages.

http://lmss.sali.org/RDJxZ2vqqnde5q8ti6P.label: Impression Evidence
http://lmss.sali.org/RDJxZ2vqqnde5q8ti6P.definition: Impression evidence refers to marks, patterns, or imprints left on surfaces that can be studied and analyzed to derive information about the object or tool that made them. Examples include shoeprints, tire treads, and tool marks. Such evidence can be instrumental in criminal investigations, as it can link a particular object or individual to a crime scene. Detailed analysis of these impressions can reveal unique characteristics or wear patterns that can be matched to specific sources.

http://lmss.sali.org/RDJy67uuHSmMFfjfpev.label: Best Interest of the Child Claim
http://lmss.sali.org/RDJy67uuHSmMFfjfpev.definition: A Best Interest of the Child Claim is a legal argument presented in family court, typically during custody or visitation disputes, where one party asserts that a particular custody arrangement or decision serves the child's best interests. This claim focuses on the child's welfare and well-being, considering factors such as their emotional, physical, and educational needs, the stability of each parent's home, and their relationship with both parents. Courts prioritize the best interests of the child when making custody and visitation determinations to ensure their safety and well-being.

http://lmss.sali.org/RDJyLaQc804aQ8QTjdA.label: Enurement Clause
http://lmss.sali.org/RDJyLaQc804aQ8QTjdA.definition: An Enurement Clause is a provision in a contract that ensures the benefits or obligations of the contract extend to third parties who were not originally parties to the contract.

http://lmss.sali.org/RDJyQQ2d7F3O273pz23.label: Fixed Costs
http://lmss.sali.org/RDJyQQ2d7F3O273pz23.definition: Fixed costs are expenses that do not change regardless of the business's production levels or service levels. Examples include rent, salaries of permanent staff, and insurance premiums, and these costs are incurred even if the business has zero output.

http://lmss.sali.org/RDK00RGn4D8WBqOyOXq.label: Legislative Proceedings
http://lmss.sali.org/RDK00RGn4D8WBqOyOXq.definition: Legislative Proceedings refer to the formal discussions and decision-making processes carried out by a governing body, such as a parliament or congress, in order to create or amend laws.

http://lmss.sali.org/RDK1HhTVsPM0kA6teSZ.label: Application for Order Waiving Requirement for Business Evaluation
http://lmss.sali.org/RDK1HhTVsPM0kA6teSZ.definition: An Application for Order Waiving Requirement for Business Evaluation is a legal document submitted in bankruptcy proceedings requesting exemption from the requirement to evaluate the debtor's business.

http://lmss.sali.org/RDK1QEdQg1T8B5HQqMK.label: Service
http://lmss.sali.org/RDK1QEdQg1T8B5HQqMK.definition: The legal work performed, usually by a Legal Services Provider, in the course of a legal matter.

http://lmss.sali.org/RDK1m7oO4kL4ZQ5IhOo.label: Pennsylvania Court of Common Pleas -  Susquehanna County
http://lmss.sali.org/RDK1m7oO4kL4ZQ5IhOo.definition: The Pennsylvania Court of Common Pleas - Susquehanna County is a specific court within the Pennsylvania Court of Common Pleas system, which is responsible for administering legal proceedings in Susquehanna County, Pennsylvania.

http://lmss.sali.org/RDK3BH34ImngQeFHXkz.label: Labor and Delivery Malpractice
http://lmss.sali.org/RDK3BH34ImngQeFHXkz.definition: Negligent or improper medical care provided during the process of childbirth, resulting in harm or injury to the mother or child, falling under the category of medical malpractice claims.

http://lmss.sali.org/RDK3ploePpyFDgIkSzb.label: Last Will and Testament
http://lmss.sali.org/RDK3ploePpyFDgIkSzb.definition: A Last Will and Testament is a legal document that outlines a person's wishes for the distribution of their property and assets after their death, and is a type of Trusts and Estate Planning Document.

http://lmss.sali.org/RDK6KqszFBwtJBxdJto.label: Squash
http://lmss.sali.org/RDK6KqszFBwtJBxdJto.definition: Squash refers to a diverse group of fruit vegetables from the Cucurbitaceae family, known for their various shapes, sizes, and flavors. They are categorized into summer and winter types, and are valued for their culinary versatility, nutritional benefits, including vitamins A and C, fiber, and antioxidants.

http://lmss.sali.org/RDK6eFy9n1upjAdRoNb.label: Tax Law Regulatory Objectives
http://lmss.sali.org/RDK6eFy9n1upjAdRoNb.definition: Tax law regulatory objectives encompass the fundamental principles and considerations surrounding taxation.

http://lmss.sali.org/RDKAbM3LW2xY7EihJPQ.label: Registered Securities
http://lmss.sali.org/RDKAbM3LW2xY7EihJPQ.definition: Registered Securities are financial instruments recorded in the name of the owner on the books of the issuer or the issuer's registrar. Normally, these securities can only be transferred to another owner when endorsed by the registered owner, ensuring a clear record of ownership.

http://lmss.sali.org/RDKBHehSWDsJ1u1ZjfM.label: Testimonial Evidence
http://lmss.sali.org/RDKBHehSWDsJ1u1ZjfM.definition: Testimonial Evidence is a type of evidence that is presented in the form of a witness's oral or written statement under oath, which is offered to prove the truth of the matter asserted. This evidence is based on the witness's personal knowledge or experience and is subject to cross-examination by the opposing party.

http://lmss.sali.org/RDKGeTDagCQ714D5C4s.label: Anxiety and Obsessive-Compulsive Disorders
http://lmss.sali.org/RDKGeTDagCQ714D5C4s.definition: Anxiety and Obsessive-Compulsive Disorders are characterized by excessive anxiety, worry, apprehension, and fear, or by avoidance of feelings, thoughts, activities, objects, places, or people.  Symptoms and signs may include restlessness, difficulty concentrating, hyper-vigilance, muscle tension, sleep disturbance, fatigue, panic attacks, obsessions and compulsions, constant thoughts and fears about safety, and frequent physical complaints.

http://lmss.sali.org/RDKHz2tUvUDYTa1DlEF.label: Foster Care
http://lmss.sali.org/RDKHz2tUvUDYTa1DlEF.definition: Foster care is a system in which a minor has been placed into a ward, group home, or private home of a state-certified caregiver, referred to as a "foster parent". This placement is often arranged through the government or a social service agency, usually due to the child's home environment being deemed unsafe or unsuitable.
sources: From LIST: Legal Issues Taxonomy — https://taxonomy.legal/

http://lmss.sali.org/RDKJ7nEqeDxNDRxI2Wq.label: Statute of Limitations
http://lmss.sali.org/RDKJ7nEqeDxNDRxI2Wq.definition: A Statute of Limitations is a legal defense that sets a specific time limit for bringing a lawsuit or criminal charges, after which the claim or charges cannot be pursued.

http://lmss.sali.org/RDKNVxICQDLTVRhliBp.label: Motion for Turnover of Property
http://lmss.sali.org/RDKNVxICQDLTVRhliBp.definition: A Motion for Turnover of Property is a legal request made in a bankruptcy case, asking the court to order the transfer of specific property from the debtor to the trustee or creditor.

http://lmss.sali.org/RDKSHk0fleH3UJIiS4l.label: Domain Name Dispute Resolution Practice
http://lmss.sali.org/RDKSHk0fleH3UJIiS4l.definition: Domain Name Dispute Resolution Practice refers to the set of procedures and guidelines followed to resolve conflicts over domain name registrations. This practice typically involves arbitration or mediation processes under policies like the Uniform Domain-Name Dispute-Resolution Policy (UDRP) to address issues such as cybersquatting and trademark infringement.

http://lmss.sali.org/RDKZpAgUjHtS3sp8YcG.label: Teen Market Segment
http://lmss.sali.org/RDKZpAgUjHtS3sp8YcG.definition: The teen market segment refers to a division of the market that is specifically targeted towards teenagers as consumers. This segment encompasses products, services, and marketing strategies that are designed to cater to the unique needs, preferences, and interests of teenagers, taking into account factors such as social trends, lifestyle choices, and identity exploration.

http://lmss.sali.org/RDKaBk2mcAWgrFpk174.label: Oregon Circuit Court - Hood River County
http://lmss.sali.org/RDKaBk2mcAWgrFpk174.definition: Oregon Circuit Court - Hood River County: A specific court within the Oregon Circuit Court system that has jurisdiction over legal proceedings in Hood River County.

http://lmss.sali.org/RDKbgwmiQQPOKcSWXQs.label: Adverse Co-Party
http://lmss.sali.org/RDKbgwmiQQPOKcSWXQs.definition: A co-party in a litigation or transactional matter who, although formally aligned on the same side (such as co-plaintiffs or co-defendants), is acting contrary to the interests of a specific client in the same proceeding or deal. This adverse action may involve conflicting positions, strategies, or goals within the shared matter.

http://lmss.sali.org/RDKkGQn6tcvXzCQnMaS.label: Havasupai Tribe of the Havasupai Reservation

http://lmss.sali.org/RDKm1RXP9FfvhLzWjyn.label: Remedies in Property Law
http://lmss.sali.org/RDKm1RXP9FfvhLzWjyn.definition: Remedies in Property Law are legal actions or procedures used to enforce property rights and resolve disputes over property ownership or possession. Each remedy (e.g., foreclosure, seizure, attachment) serves to protect the interests of the property holder or creditor and is governed by specific laws and regulations.

http://lmss.sali.org/RDKpHba5IfYCfGzQFwo.label: Georgia District Court - Fayette County
http://lmss.sali.org/RDKpHba5IfYCfGzQFwo.definition: Georgia District Court - Fayette County: A court of law in the state of Georgia with jurisdiction over legal cases within Fayette County.

http://lmss.sali.org/RDL012eXNoS65Wz1Bek.label: California Court of Appeal - 4th Dist.
http://lmss.sali.org/RDL012eXNoS65Wz1Bek.definition: The California Court of Appeal - 4th Dist. is a specific division of the California Court of Appeal that hears appeals from trial courts in the fourth appellate district of California.

http://lmss.sali.org/RDL7pg0w01PEka8zAYF.label: Large Language Model
http://lmss.sali.org/RDL7pg0w01PEka8zAYF.definition: A Large Language Model (LLM) is a class of language models that utilize deep learning algorithms and are trained on extensive textual datasets, often spanning multiple terabytes in size. While most LLMs can generate text, some are designed to form compressed representations of inputs for tasks like classification or question answering.

http://lmss.sali.org/RDLA7xQQZfuDjATh4LO.label: Urdu
http://lmss.sali.org/RDLA7xQQZfuDjATh4LO.definition: Urdu (Language) is a structured system of communication consisting of grammar and vocabulary, primarily spoken in Pakistan and India.

http://lmss.sali.org/RDLAJyBXKhid99OheQ7.label: Motion to Extend Time to File Appellee Designation of Reporters Transcript
http://lmss.sali.org/RDLAJyBXKhid99OheQ7.definition: A request made to the appellate court to allow additional time for the appellee to submit the designated reporters' transcript.

http://lmss.sali.org/RDLANHrFj8nfaiNIalX.label: Self-Defense
http://lmss.sali.org/RDLANHrFj8nfaiNIalX.definition: Self-defense is a legal doctrine that allows an individual to use reasonable force to protect themselves or others from imminent physical harm or danger. It is generally considered a justifiable defense in criminal cases when a person believes they are facing a genuine threat and uses force in a proportionate and necessary manner to defend themselves.

http://lmss.sali.org/RDLC4OUTQwKGImbneCf.label: Altaic languages
http://lmss.sali.org/RDLC4OUTQwKGImbneCf.definition: A group of languages including Turkish, Mongolian, and Manchu, among others, that share certain grammatical and phonetic features and are primarily spoken in Central Asia and parts of Eastern Europe.

http://lmss.sali.org/RDLEwvLaIWPi5S2pyK6.label: URL of Legal Services Provider
http://lmss.sali.org/RDLEwvLaIWPi5S2pyK6.definition: A URL of Legal Services Provider is a web address that identifies an organization providing legal services.

http://lmss.sali.org/RDLIpK2R8t5eS7LDT63.label: Auctioneer
http://lmss.sali.org/RDLIpK2R8t5eS7LDT63.definition: A person who sells goods at a public auction.

http://lmss.sali.org/RDLJFOLdDrD89A25lPq.label: Frustration of Purpose Doctrine
http://lmss.sali.org/RDLJFOLdDrD89A25lPq.definition: The Frustration of Purpose Doctrine is a legal defense in civil litigation that allows a party to be excused from performing their contractual obligations when an unforeseen event occurs that completely undermines the purpose of the contract.

http://lmss.sali.org/RDLOreSz8ONDugOdcgD.label: Attached Hereto Clause
http://lmss.sali.org/RDLOreSz8ONDugOdcgD.definition: A clause in a contract that specifies certain documents or items that are attached to and made a part of the contract.

http://lmss.sali.org/RDLPlYoTdnG7grfJWdM.label: Angika
http://lmss.sali.org/RDLPlYoTdnG7grfJWdM.definition: Angika is a language that is a member of the Language top-level class and is spoken in the Indian state of Bihar.

http://lmss.sali.org/RDLQ3sCxs7nibjVlt55.label: Georgia Superior Court - Jones County
http://lmss.sali.org/RDLQ3sCxs7nibjVlt55.definition: A court of general jurisdiction in Jones County, Georgia, with authority over civil and criminal cases within its geographical jurisdiction.

http://lmss.sali.org/RDLQDOiX6GNalq6NwrY.label: Chapter 13 Bankruptcy Plan
http://lmss.sali.org/RDLQDOiX6GNalq6NwrY.definition: A Chapter 13 Bankruptcy Plan is a legal document that outlines a debtor's proposed repayment plan to creditors under Chapter 13 bankruptcy, which allows individuals with regular income to reorganize their debts and keep their property.

http://lmss.sali.org/RDLSiIZBb3Cx0FiRItl.label: Aleut
http://lmss.sali.org/RDLSiIZBb3Cx0FiRItl.definition: Aleut (Language) is a structured system of communication spoken by the Aleut people, which belongs to the Language top-level class in the context of legal matters.

http://lmss.sali.org/RDLTyL6ODZoS6Th2kl5.label: 535 Death Penalty (PACER NoS)
http://lmss.sali.org/RDLTyL6ODZoS6Th2kl5.definition: Action by a federal or state prisoner challenging a death sentence.

http://lmss.sali.org/RDLXknd7NhCpnyqxaUT.label: Petition for Visa for Intermittent Intra-Company Transferee
http://lmss.sali.org/RDLXknd7NhCpnyqxaUT.definition: The "Petition for Visa for Intermittent Intra-Company Transferee" typically refers to the L-1 visa category in the United States. This visa is used for employees who work in a managerial, executive, or specialized knowledge capacity and are being transferred within the same company from a foreign office to a U.S. office on an intermittent basis. The employer must file a Form I-129 petition with U.S. Citizenship and Immigration Services (USCIS) to seek approval for the L-1 visa

http://lmss.sali.org/RDLdmfBT7ttR0UhaZsq.label: Chignik Bay Tribal Council (Native Village of Chignik)

http://lmss.sali.org/RDLmn3zQET0KpZTPNJb.label: Insurance Representation
http://lmss.sali.org/RDLmn3zQET0KpZTPNJb.definition: Insurance Representation is a provision in merger and acquisition agreements where the selling party confirms the existence, sufficiency, and status of insurance policies held by the target entity. This representation assures the buyer that the target has adequate insurance coverage in place to protect against potential liabilities or losses, and that there are no material lapses or issues with these policies.

http://lmss.sali.org/RDLoC8ihhC6ueFffAIU.label: Co-Branding Agreement
http://lmss.sali.org/RDLoC8ihhC6ueFffAIU.definition: A co-branding agreement is a legal contract between two or more companies that outlines the terms and conditions of a joint marketing campaign or product collaboration.

http://lmss.sali.org/RDLrr0QnPzgK38sYlXg.label: Debtor's Certification in Support of Discharge
http://lmss.sali.org/RDLrr0QnPzgK38sYlXg.definition: A Debtor's Certification in Support of Discharge is a document filed in a bankruptcy case by the debtor, attesting to the accuracy of the information provided in the bankruptcy petition and supporting documents.

http://lmss.sali.org/RDLuS9uU4PbVxHlpO8V.label: UTBMS MC00 Due Diligence and Disclosure Schedules
http://lmss.sali.org/RDLuS9uU4PbVxHlpO8V.definition: A category within the UTBMS Mergers and Acquisitions (M&A) class that pertains to the due diligence and disclosure schedules involved in such transactions.

http://lmss.sali.org/RDLwMGk81VgissVsVE3.label: Yankton Sioux Tribe of South Dakota

http://lmss.sali.org/RDM0lGCVtkIa8r6oJzU.label: Warehouseman or Carrier Liability for Goods
http://lmss.sali.org/RDM0lGCVtkIa8r6oJzU.definition: The legal responsibility of a warehouseman or carrier for the goods they are holding or transporting, which falls under the broader category of agent liability.

http://lmss.sali.org/RDM1qeBjyKPU0FCQHOy.label: Hungarian
http://lmss.sali.org/RDM1qeBjyKPU0FCQHOy.definition: A language spoken in Hungary and by Hungarian communities worldwide.

http://lmss.sali.org/RDM2DW9jiNezwy5XHki.label: Michigan District Court -  Wayne County
http://lmss.sali.org/RDM2DW9jiNezwy5XHki.definition: Michigan District Court - Wayne County: A court of limited jurisdiction in the state of Michigan that handles civil and criminal cases within Wayne County.

http://lmss.sali.org/RDM4k8t0O3hy93vQwQz.label: Issuer
http://lmss.sali.org/RDM4k8t0O3hy93vQwQz.definition: An issuer is a legal entity that develops, registers and sells securities to finance its operations. Issuers may be corporations, investment trusts, or domestic or foreign governments.

http://lmss.sali.org/RDM5pRFuWAnNukzEPxf.label: Request for Evidence
http://lmss.sali.org/RDM5pRFuWAnNukzEPxf.definition: A Request for Evidence (RFE) in the context of immigration is a document issued by the government agency (e.g., United States Citizenship and Immigration Services (USCIS)) when an immigration application or petition lacks sufficient evidence or documentation. The RFE requests additional information or documentation from the applicant or petitioner to make a decision on the case.

http://lmss.sali.org/RDMCKTIUqYeWtfiRQUU.label: Probate due to Neglect/Abandonment
http://lmss.sali.org/RDMCKTIUqYeWtfiRQUU.definition: Probate due to Neglect/Abandonment refers to the legal process of distributing the assets of a deceased person who died without a will or heirs due to neglect or abandonment.

http://lmss.sali.org/RDMDwRdvGV1SmoM2o59.label: General Representations and Warranties
http://lmss.sali.org/RDMDwRdvGV1SmoM2o59.definition: A General Representation and Warranty is a statement made by a party in a legal matter that asserts the truthfulness and accuracy of certain facts or conditions, without any specific limitations or exceptions, and which may be subject to a Material Adverse Effect (MAE) Qualification.

http://lmss.sali.org/RDMHSA6grqlpIvoXjTO.label: Washington Superior Court - Wahkiakum County
http://lmss.sali.org/RDMHSA6grqlpIvoXjTO.definition: Washington Superior Court - Wahkiakum County refers to a specific court within the Washington Superior Court system that has jurisdiction over legal matters in Wahkiakum County.

http://lmss.sali.org/RDMIFgVwND9pPCV8Mb2.label: Mental Health Claims
http://lmss.sali.org/RDMIFgVwND9pPCV8Mb2.definition: Mental health claims involve legal processes related to an individual's psychological well-being, often concerning the need for treatment or intervention. Commitments to mental health facilities can be voluntary, where an individual willingly seeks treatment, or involuntary, where an individual is mandated to receive treatment due to potential harm to themselves or others, based on legal criteria and professional assessments.

http://lmss.sali.org/RDMJJ2pHLHHjGKbC1xD.label: Trespassing Livestock Causing Harm
http://lmss.sali.org/RDMJJ2pHLHHjGKbC1xD.definition: The concept of Trespassing Livestock Causing Harm refers to the legal claim that arises when someone's animals enter another person's property without permission and cause damage or injury.

http://lmss.sali.org/RDMNx0AK0j8Rc7MLtq2.label: Obscenity
http://lmss.sali.org/RDMNx0AK0j8Rc7MLtq2.definition: Obscenity refers to a criminal offense that involves the distribution or display of materials that are considered offensive or indecent according to community standards.

http://lmss.sali.org/RDMSaAtom7aKKKg3DZg.label: Jaywalking Claim
http://lmss.sali.org/RDMSaAtom7aKKKg3DZg.definition: A Jaywalking Claim involves allegations that a pedestrian has violated traffic regulations by crossing a street outside of designated crosswalks or against traffic signals, creating potential hazards for both themselves and motorists.

http://lmss.sali.org/RDMTIY9dbpdtPFxH3BM.label: Use of Premises Clause
http://lmss.sali.org/RDMTIY9dbpdtPFxH3BM.definition: The Use of Premises Clause is a provision in a contract that outlines the permitted use of a specific property or space by the tenant or lessee.

http://lmss.sali.org/RDMTq4YXBz2Kmxr08XW.label: 861 HIA (PACER NoS)
http://lmss.sali.org/RDMTq4YXBz2Kmxr08XW.definition: Action filed with regard to social security benefits associated with Health Insurance Part A Medicare

http://lmss.sali.org/RDMUOtKEW0m4knNvedj.label: Ulcerative Colitis
http://lmss.sali.org/RDMUOtKEW0m4knNvedj.definition: Ulcerative colitis is a chronic inflammatory bowel disease characterized by inflammation and ulceration of the lining of the colon and rectum. This condition primarily affects the mucosal layer, leading to symptoms such as abdominal pain, diarrhea with blood or pus, and weight loss, and may require ongoing medical treatment or surgical intervention, such as colectomy.

http://lmss.sali.org/RDMUndZU5gtYHS21t5e.label: Motion to Exclude Testimony
http://lmss.sali.org/RDMUndZU5gtYHS21t5e.definition: A Motion to Exclude Testimony is a formal request made to a court to prevent certain testimony from being presented as evidence during a trial or hearing.

http://lmss.sali.org/RDMUsjTZ7MYlmJzfXob.label: Lease Obligations
http://lmss.sali.org/RDMUsjTZ7MYlmJzfXob.definition: Lease Obligations refer to the financial and contractual responsibilities that a lessee must fulfill as part of a lease agreement. These often include timely payment of rent, adherence to maintenance and use provisions, and compliance with any terms for lease termination or renewal

http://lmss.sali.org/RDMiMuoKB1tpvbIZ4A4.label: Buyer In Breach Liable for Real Estate Broker's Commission
http://lmss.sali.org/RDMiMuoKB1tpvbIZ4A4.definition: If a buyer fails to fulfill their obligations under a real estate contract, they may be held responsible for paying the commission owed to the broker who facilitated the sale.

http://lmss.sali.org/RDMlfBHhw2Mfk0FBrVC.label: Life Insurance Policy
http://lmss.sali.org/RDMlfBHhw2Mfk0FBrVC.definition: A life insurance policy is a contract between an insurance company and a policyholder that provides a financial payout to designated beneficiaries upon the death of the insured individual. The policy often requires the payment of regular premiums in exchange for the death benefit, and may include other features like investment growth or cash value.

http://lmss.sali.org/RDMllTEq28i1rFUt6SW.label: Florida Circuit Court - Holmes County - 14th Circuit Court
http://lmss.sali.org/RDMllTEq28i1rFUt6SW.definition: A court located in Holmes County, Florida that is part of the larger Florida Circuit Court system.

http://lmss.sali.org/RDMmVnDBUmOnVx8i4Zp.label: Escrow Agreement
http://lmss.sali.org/RDMmVnDBUmOnVx8i4Zp.definition: An Escrow Agreement is a legal contract between two parties where a third party holds and manages assets or funds until the conditions of the agreement are met.

http://lmss.sali.org/RDMmocc9Ine34BK9vSk.label: Trustworthy AI
http://lmss.sali.org/RDMmocc9Ine34BK9vSk.definition: Trustworthy AI is an AI system characterized by three main components: (1) it must be lawful, ensuring compliance with all applicable laws and regulations, (2) it should be ethical, demonstrating respect for and adherence to ethical principles and values, and (3) it should be robust, both technically and socially, to prevent unintentional harm. Trustworthy AI concerns the trustworthiness of the AI system itself and includes all processes and actors involved in the AI system's life cycle, emphasizing respect for human rights and democratic values.

http://lmss.sali.org/RDMogej8AdNSlkztHiK.label: Current Financial Obligations
http://lmss.sali.org/RDMogej8AdNSlkztHiK.definition: Current Financial Obligations, also known as Current Liabilities, are debts or obligations that a company is expected to settle within one fiscal year or operating cycle, whichever is longer. These can include accounts payable, short-term loans, and other debts that are due within a short timeframe, and they are listed on a company's balance sheet.

http://lmss.sali.org/RDMrBgmf7sx8XGaMk7z.label: Florida Circuit Court - Pinellas County - 6th Circuit Court
http://lmss.sali.org/RDMrBgmf7sx8XGaMk7z.definition: A court located in Pinellas County, Florida that is part of the larger Florida Circuit Court system.

http://lmss.sali.org/RDMvlybB2Ds3VpLsrk7.label: Mootness
http://lmss.sali.org/RDMvlybB2Ds3VpLsrk7.definition: Mootness refers to a legal principle where a case is deemed irrelevant because it no longer presents an ongoing issue, or the parties involved no longer have a legally recognizable interest in the outcome. When a case becomes moot, courts generally dismiss it, as there is no longer a "live" controversy to resolve

http://lmss.sali.org/RDN125qcdfOhqnuRT6m.label: Forward-looking MAE Standard - "Could reasonably be expected to" Language
http://lmss.sali.org/RDN125qcdfOhqnuRT6m.definition: A Forward-looking MAE Standard with "Could reasonably be expected to" Language is a legal concept that refers to a standard used in contracts to determine whether a particular event or circumstance could reasonably be expected to have a material adverse effect on a party's business, financial condition, or operations.

http://lmss.sali.org/RDN7bio8UsCmImnSv1J.label: Negligent Retention
http://lmss.sali.org/RDN7bio8UsCmImnSv1J.definition: The concept of Negligent Retention refers to a legal claim that an employer was negligent in retaining an employee who they knew or should have known posed a risk of harm to others.

http://lmss.sali.org/RDN7pZcrfOnzR6Jruat.label: Total Tax on Fees
http://lmss.sali.org/RDN7pZcrfOnzR6Jruat.definition: The Total Tax on Fees is a subcategory of Tax Detail in the Engagement Terms ontology, referring to the complete amount of tax imposed on legal service fees.

http://lmss.sali.org/RDN8CVqeiDlOeHJO8Oe.label: Climate-Based Market Segment
http://lmss.sali.org/RDN8CVqeiDlOeHJO8Oe.definition: A climate-based market segment refers to a group of consumers or businesses categorized based on the climatic conditions of their geographical location. This segmentation helps businesses tailor their products, services, and marketing strategies to suit the specific needs and preferences of people living in areas with similar climatic characteristics

http://lmss.sali.org/RDNArIic0aVNyOAKTSS.label: Umbundu
http://lmss.sali.org/RDNArIic0aVNyOAKTSS.definition: A Bantu language spoken in Angola, characterized by its use of click consonants and other unique phonetic features.

http://lmss.sali.org/RDNBuSf0mzFPvmzSa1Z.label: Breathalyzer Test
http://lmss.sali.org/RDNBuSf0mzFPvmzSa1Z.definition: A Breathalyzer test is a procedure that measures the concentration of alcohol in an individual's breath to determine their blood alcohol content (BAC). This test is commonly used by law enforcement agencies to assess if a driver is operating a vehicle under the influence of alcohol.

http://lmss.sali.org/RDNC62XHr3WDD7XO7B5.label: Hiligaynon
http://lmss.sali.org/RDNC62XHr3WDD7XO7B5.definition: A language spoken in the Western Visayas region of the Philippines, specifically in the provinces of Iloilo, Guimaras, and Negros Occidental.

http://lmss.sali.org/RDNDZH2X3OVk6FwdmXY.label: Termination Without Cause by the Company Clause
http://lmss.sali.org/RDNDZH2X3OVk6FwdmXY.definition: A Termination Without Cause by the Company Clause is a provision in a contract that allows a company to end the agreement without providing a reason.

http://lmss.sali.org/RDNJ4NKjJEf08oWXQI1.label: Virgin Islands Territorial Court
http://lmss.sali.org/RDNJ4NKjJEf08oWXQI1.definition: The Virgin Islands Territorial Court is a court system within the Virgin Islands Territory Courts that has jurisdiction over certain legal matters in the United States Virgin Islands.

http://lmss.sali.org/RDNOTESvIFXoyO4t8nS.label: School Zone Violation Claim
http://lmss.sali.org/RDNOTESvIFXoyO4t8nS.definition: A School Zone Violation Claim involves allegations that a driver has failed to adhere to specific traffic rules in a school zone, such as speed limits or stopping requirements, endangering the safety of children and other pedestrians.

http://lmss.sali.org/RDNOqfCVAhPu7lEHc6g.label: Living
http://lmss.sali.org/RDNOqfCVAhPu7lEHc6g.definition: Living refers to the state of being alive and having the capacity to perform vital functions, such as breathing and circulating blood, as opposed to being deceased or non-living.

http://lmss.sali.org/RDNWWH9RIbJqVpU8sO0.label: Architectural, Engineering, and Related Services Industry
http://lmss.sali.org/RDNWWH9RIbJqVpU8sO0.definition: This industry group comprises establishments primarily engaged in architectural, engineering, and related services, such as drafting services, building inspection services, geophysical surveying and mapping services, surveying and mapping (except geophysical) services, and testing services.

http://lmss.sali.org/RDNaE3PFsXDfIudTq7w.label: Judicial Opinion
http://lmss.sali.org/RDNaE3PFsXDfIudTq7w.definition: A judicial opinion is a written statement by a judge or a panel of judges explaining the decision reached in a legal case, typically including the legal reasoning and principles applied to the case.

http://lmss.sali.org/RDNcVSAeA3f0hh7RzDW.label: Georgia Superior Court - Tattnall County
http://lmss.sali.org/RDNcVSAeA3f0hh7RzDW.definition: A court of general jurisdiction in the state of Georgia that has authority over legal matters within Tattnall County.

http://lmss.sali.org/RDNoThgrXS0EUafEvLb.label: Georgia Superior Court - Walker County
http://lmss.sali.org/RDNoThgrXS0EUafEvLb.definition: Georgia Superior Court - Walker County: A court of general jurisdiction in the state of Georgia that has authority over civil and criminal cases within Walker County.

http://lmss.sali.org/RDNrS2sV3g20bYF8ec8.label: General Partner
http://lmss.sali.org/RDNrS2sV3g20bYF8ec8.definition: A general partner is an owner of a partnership. Often, a general partner either plays an active role in the company's daily operations or is a managing partner. A general partner for a business can act on the company's behalf.

http://lmss.sali.org/RDNsW4JqaHcQ9KPtpXL.label: Requirements for Public Benefits
http://lmss.sali.org/RDNsW4JqaHcQ9KPtpXL.definition: Requirements for public benefits refer to the conditions or activities that an individual or family must fulfill to qualify for or continue receiving financial assistance or services from a government program. These can include mandates for job searches, participation in educational or vocational training programs, or completion of specific plans aimed at improving self-sufficiency. Failure to meet these requirements may result in reduction, suspension, or termination of benefits.

http://lmss.sali.org/RDNshZ3PkToac7qKDzE.label: WC210 Pleadings
http://lmss.sali.org/RDNshZ3PkToac7qKDzE.definition: Drafting/editing/filing all pleadings, reviewing opposing pleadings, counter-claims and third party complaints, research for pleadings, preparing/drafting/filing workers' compensation state forms and supporting Memorandum of Law, preparing affidavits/attorney affirmations, prepare communication with adjuster/employer regarding analysis/summary of pleadings/state forms

http://lmss.sali.org/RDNwG4cfweNsjq5ZDtw.label: New York City Court - Syracuse
http://lmss.sali.org/RDNwG4cfweNsjq5ZDtw.definition: A court located in Syracuse, New York that operates under the jurisdiction of the New York City Court.

http://lmss.sali.org/RDNy9j94ASJKn7liLm1.label: Litigation Collaboration Management
http://lmss.sali.org/RDNy9j94ASJKn7liLm1.definition: Litigation Collaboration Management refers to the process of managing and coordinating the efforts of multiple parties involved in a legal dispute, with the goal of achieving a successful outcome.

http://lmss.sali.org/RDNzfP8C4t6kAYGZbJX.label: Company Blanket Petition
http://lmss.sali.org/RDNzfP8C4t6kAYGZbJX.definition: The "Company Blanket Petition" refers to the L-1 Blanket Petition in the United States, which allows certain multinational companies to streamline the process of transferring employees to the U.S. under the L-1A or L-1B visa categories. With a blanket petition approval, the company can bypass the individual L-1 petition process for each employee and instead submit a simplified application to facilitate multiple employee transfers.

http://lmss.sali.org/RDO2UGTCtFZdU1kQqbs.definition: A Motion to Delay Discharge is a request made in a bankruptcy case to extend the time period before the debtor is released from their debts, typically to allow for completion of certain requirements or to address objections from creditors.

http://lmss.sali.org/RDO3UKXcvzCX1v6RIJE.definition: "Wire Transfer" refers to the electronic transfer of funds from one financial institution or account to another, executed via a network of banking institutions or transfer service providers. This method of transferring money is commonly used for both domestic and international transactions and is generally considered secure and fast.

http://lmss.sali.org/RDOQpX5t5sVf55UPK2C.definition: A "Human Trafficking Claim" pertains to the allegation or assertion that individuals have been recruited, transported, harbored, or received, often through force, coercion, or deception, for the purpose of exploitation. Such claims challenge violations of human rights and can encompass various forms of exploitation including, but not limited to, forced labor, sexual exploitation, and organ trafficking.

http://lmss.sali.org/RDOVXukylaJyAh50ONZ.definition: A Timekeeper ID is a unique identifier assigned to an individual who provides legal services, indicating their role and responsibilities within a legal engagement.

http://lmss.sali.org/RDOWSerdWZR3POAsYxg.definition: A Financial Statement is a formal record of the financial activities and position of a business, organization, or individual, typically presented in structured manner for a specific time period. http://lmss.sali.org/RDOcmtJjE35asuo2CYD.definition: Rundi is a structured system of communication that consists of grammar and vocabulary, and is a member of the language family.

http://lmss.sali.org/RDOfHufoKKV4QprPsIq.definition: An L-2 Petition allows the immediate family members of L-1 visa holders, specifically their spouses and unmarried children under 21, to accompany or join the primary visa holder in the U.S. This petition facilitates the entry and stay of dependents of L-1 visa holders.

http://lmss.sali.org/RDOgxjWbgT1G7Mx1GDe.definition: A Motion or Filing to Disqualify Decisionmaker is a legal request made by a party to remove a judge, arbitrator, or other decisionmaker from a case due to a perceived conflict of interest or bias.

http://lmss.sali.org/RDOm7uyuCKhvuGGPF0u.definition: Utilization is a metric often used in service industries to measure the percentage of a professional's working hours that are engaged in revenue-generating activities (billable). It is calculated by dividing the billable hours by the total available working hours. Utilization it usually expressed as a percentage, used to assess individual, team, or workforce efficiency and capacity utilization.

http://lmss.sali.org/RDOoYq5UsqIy3nBTVUn.label: State Government Representative
http://lmss.sali.org/RDOoYq5UsqIy3nBTVUn.definition: A State Government Representative is an elected or appointed official who serves in the government of a state, province, or similar sub-national administrative division. http://lmss.sali.org/RDOppPCupWvkmNYt9jF.label: Fair and True Reporting Privilege
http://lmss.sali.org/RDOppPCupWvkmNYt9jF.definition: The Fair and True Reporting Privilege is a legal immunity and privilege that protects journalists and media outlets from being sued for defamation when reporting on matters of public interest, as long as they report accurately and in good faith.

http://lmss.sali.org/RDOq8HJJl8YdcwBdCZm.definition: A confidentiality clause is a provision in a contract that requires one or more parties to keep certain information confidential and not disclose it to others.

http://lmss.sali.org/RDOsWAgVqSIizWGJ68f.label: PA550 Continuing Application Preparation - International
http://lmss.sali.org/RDOsWAgVqSIizWGJ68f.definition: All actions associated with completing a continuing patent application (claiming priority to an earlier-filed application in the same country, but without adding new disclosure) that are to be filed outside the ('domestic') home country or region of the applicant, including translations, review of any invention disclosure materials or parent applications, drafting of application including pre-filing revision of any parent applications, preparation and execution of formal documents (such as assignments, declarations, information disclosure statements, transmittals, and biological deposits) filing of application, and reporting to the client. Also includes PCT National Phase entry where the parent PCT International Application was previously filed in another country. For PCT National Phase entry in the applicant's home country, use PA300. Note that (so-called "continuation-in-part") patent applications extending the scope of the disclosure (or so-called "new matter" in the U.S.) in an earlier-filed application are included under PA520- PA540. Also that government fees and other external expenses are included under E100

http://lmss.sali.org/RDOtom7nYG8Lf6j7zEr.label: Common-Law Marriage Creation Event
http://lmss.sali.org/RDOtom7nYG8Lf6j7zEr.definition: Common-law marriage refers to a type of informal marriage where two individuals cohabit and present themselves as a married couple without having undergone a formal legal marriage ceremony. http://lmss.sali.org/RDQ8w43q2ST3z8GpDUI.label: Freedom of Assembly
http://lmss.sali.org/RDQ8w43q2ST3z8GpDUI.definition: A freedom of assembly claim is a legal action initiated by an individual or group alleging that their right to freedom of assembly, as protected by the First Amendment of the United States Constitution, has been violated by the government or a government actor. A freedom of assembly claim may arise in various contexts, such as when a government body enacts a law or regulation that unduly restricts assembly, when a permit for a peaceful protest or gathering is unfairly denied, or when an assembly is disbanded or interfered with by law enforcement without just cause.

http://lmss.sali.org/RDQfVpnn3USyDLsqbJy.label: Employer Fault Set-off
http://lmss.sali.org/RDQfVpnn3USyDLsqbJy.definition: Employer fault set-off diminishes the amount of damages a defendant is liable for based on the comparative fault of a plaintiff's employer and/or co-employees, as well as a certain set-off from the Workers' Compensation benefits paid to date.

http://lmss.sali.org/RDQhLz0PnZB43VXzrf4.label: Furniture and Related Product Manufacturing Industry
http://lmss.sali.org/RDQhLz0PnZB43VXzrf4.definition:
Industries in the Furniture and Related Product Manufacturing subsector make furniture and related articles, such as mattresses, window blinds, cabinets, and fixtures.  The processes used in the manufacture of furniture include the cutting, bending, molding, laminating, and assembly of such materials as wood, metal, glass, plastics, and rattan.  However, the production process for furniture is not solely bending metal, cutting and shaping wood, or extruding and molding plastics.  Design and fashion trends play an important part in the production of furniture.  The integrated design of the article for both esthetic and functional qualities is also a major part of the process of manufacturing furniture.  Design services may be performed by the furniture establishment's work force or may be purchased from industrial designers.

Furniture may be made of any material, but the most common ones used in North America are metal and wood.  Furniture manufacturing establishments may specialize in making articles primarily from one material.  Some of the equipment required to make a wooden table, for example, is different from that used to make a metal one.  However, furniture is usually made from several materials.  A wooden table might have metal brackets, and a wooden chair a fabric or plastics seat.  Therefore, in NAICS, furniture initially is classified based on the type of furniture (application for which it is designed) rather than the material used.  For example, an upholstered sofa is treated as household furniture, although it may also be used in hotels or offices.

When classifying furniture according to the component material from which it is made, furniture made from more than one material is classified based on the material used in the frame, or if there is no frame, the predominant component material.  Upholstered household furniture (excluding kitchen and dining room chairs with upholstered seats) is classified without regard to the frame material.  Kitchen or dining room chairs with upholstered seats are classified according to the frame material.

Furniture may be made on a stock or custom basis and may be shipped assembled or unassembled (i.e., knockdown).  The manufacture of furniture parts and frames is included in this subsector.

Some of the processes used in furniture manufacturing are similar to processes that are used in other segments of manufacturing.  For example, cutting and assembly occurs in the production of wood trusses that are classified in Subsector 321, Wood Product Manufacturing.  However, the multiple processes that distinguish wood furniture manufacturing from wood product manufacturing warrant inclusion of wooden furniture manufacturing in the Furniture and Related Product Manufacturing subsector.  Metal furniture manufacturing uses techniques that are also employed in the manufacturing of roll formed products classified in Subsector 332, Fabricated Metal Product Manufacturing.  The molding process for plastics furniture is similar to the molding of other plastics products.  However, plastics furniture producing establishments tend to specialize in furniture.

NAICS attempts to keep furniture manufacturing together, but there are notable exceptions: concrete, ceramic, or stone furniture; seating for transportation equipment; and specialized hospital furniture (e.g., hospital beds and operating tables).  These are classified in Subsector 327, Nonmetallic Mineral Product Manufacturing; Subsector 336, Transportation Equipment Manufacturing; and Subsector 339, Miscellaneous Manufacturing, respectively.

http://lmss.sali.org/RDQmmfqXdboeJpWPNff.label: Subsequent Remedial Measures Objection
http://lmss.sali.org/RDQmmfqXdboeJpWPNff.definition: A Subsequent Remedial Measures Objection is raised when a party in a legal proceeding believes that evidence of repairs or changes made after an incident is being used to prove negligence, culpability, or a defect in a product. http://lmss.sali.org/RDQsHMOs4Yx20ic8u59.definition: The Pennsylvania Court of Common Pleas - Delaware County is a specific court within the Pennsylvania Court of Common Pleas system that has jurisdiction over civil and criminal cases within Delaware County, Pennsylvania.
